category: Scripting: Schematic API, Workspace Manager API and confirmed process commands
description: Member-level reference for the schematic scripting API (SchServer, ISch_Document sheet properties, object registration, schematic object interfaces and constants), the Workspace Manager API (IProject, IDocument, INet, IComponent members) and the server process identifiers (Server:Command strings) that are documented for use with RunProcess / Client.SendMessage.

tools.name: SchServer.ProcessControl.PreProcess / PostProcess
tools.description: Schematic counterpart of the PCB PreProcess/PostProcess pair: SchServer.ProcessControl.PreProcess(Doc, '') opens a modification session on the document and PostProcess(Doc, '') closes it, grouping all object creations/edits into one undo step and letting the compiler/robots update. Required around RegisterSchObjectInContainer and property edits.
tools.notes: Object edits should also be wrapped in SchServer.RobotManager.SendMessage(Obj.I_ObjectAddress, c_BroadCast, SCHM_BeginModify/SCHM_EndModify, c_NoEventData).

tools.name: SchServer.RobotManager.SendMessage (SCHM_BeginModify / SCHM_EndModify / SCHM_PrimitiveRegistration)
tools.description: Broadcasts schematic editor messages so that undo, the compiler and panels see programmatic changes: SCHM_BeginModify before and SCHM_EndModify after changing an existing object's properties; SCHM_PrimitiveRegistration is sent automatically by RegisterSchObjectInContainer. Destination is c_BroadCast and data c_NoEventData.
tools.usage: SchServer.RobotManager.SendMessage(Obj.I_ObjectAddress, c_BroadCast, SCHM_BeginModify, c_NoEventData); ... SchServer.RobotManager.SendMessage(Obj.I_ObjectAddress, c_BroadCast, SCHM_EndModify, c_NoEventData);
tools.notes: Without EndModify the object may not be redrawn or marked as changed.

tools.name: SchServer.GetSchDocumentByPath / LoadSchDocumentByPath / GetCurrentSchDocument
tools.description: Document accessors: GetCurrentSchDocument returns the active sheet; GetSchDocumentByPath(Path) returns the ISch_Document of an already-open sheet by full path (Nil otherwise); LoadSchDocumentByPath(Path) opens the file (without necessarily showing it) and returns its ISch_Document, useful for project-wide scripts that walk IProject.DM_LogicalDocuments.
tools.usage: SchDoc := SchServer.GetCurrentSchDocument;  SchDoc := SchServer.GetSchDocumentByPath(Path);  SchDoc := SchServer.LoadSchDocumentByPath(Path);
tools.notes: Documents loaded but not shown still need saving through WorkspaceManager:SaveObject with ObjectKind=Document and the file path.

tools.name: ISch_Document.RegisterSchObjectInContainer / UnRegisterSchObjectFromContainer
tools.description: Adds an object created by SchServer.SchObjectFactory to the sheet (or to a container such as a component for pins/parameters) and sends the registration message; UnRegisterSchObjectFromContainer removes it. Objects must have their Location and key properties set before registration for correct connectivity.

parameters.name: AObject
parameters.description: Any ISch_BasicContainer descendant (wire, net label, port, component, parameter...).

tools.notes: For component children use Cmp.AddSchObject(Param) / Cmp.RemoveSchObject instead.

tools.name: ISch_Document.PlaceSchComponent
tools.description: Places a component from a library onto the sheet in one call: PlaceSchComponent(LibraryPath, LibRef, SchObject) loads the symbol named LibRef from the given .SchLib/.IntLib and returns the placed ISch_Component handle, which can then be positioned and annotated. Simpler than building components manually with the object factory.
tools.usage: SchDoc.PlaceSchComponent(ALibraryPath : WideString; ALibRef : WideString; Var SchObject : TSchObjectHandle)

parameters.name: ALibraryPath
parameters.description: Full path of the library file.

tools.notes: The process alternative is Sch:PlacePart with Library/LibReference parameters.

tools.name: ISch_Document.ChooseLocationInteractively / ChooseRectangleInteractively
tools.description: Interactive input for schematic scripts: ChooseLocationInteractively(Location, Prompt) waits for a click and returns a TLocation (False if cancelled); ChooseRectangleInteractively(Rect, Prompt1, Prompt2) collects two corners. Used to let the user pick where generated objects go or which area to process.
tools.notes: Schematic coordinates are TCoord in DXP units (MilsToCoord works; 100 mil grid = MilsToCoord(100)).

tools.name: ISch_Document sheet properties (SheetStyle, SheetSizeX/Y, SnapGridSize, VisibleGridSize, TitleBlockOn, TemplateFileName, DocumentName)
tools.description: Document-level properties readable/writable via GetState_/SetState_ pairs or the properties: DocumentName (read-only path), SheetStyle (eSheetA4, eSheetA3, eSheetLetter, ... , custom via UseCustomSheet/CustomX/CustomY), SheetSizeX/SheetSizeY, WorkspaceOrientation (eLandscape/ePortrait), SnapGridOn/SnapGridSize, VisibleGridOn/VisibleGridSize, HotSpotGridOn/HotSpotGridSize, BorderOn, TitleBlockOn, ReferenceZonesOn, SheetZonesX/Y, TemplateFileName, ShowTemplateGraphics, SystemFont, DisplayUnit/UnitSystem, and UpdateDocumentProperties to apply changes.
tools.usage: SchDoc.SheetStyle := eSheetA3; SchDoc.SnapGridSize := MilsToCoord(100); SchDoc.TitleBlockOn := True; SchDoc.UpdateDocumentProperties; SchDoc.GraphicallyInvalidate;
tools.notes: Applying a template file is done through TemplateFileName plus the Sch:DocumentOptions/Templates processes; document parameters live in the document's parameter objects.

tools.name: ISch_Document.LockViewUpdate / UnLockViewUpdate / GraphicallyInvalidate
tools.description: Performance and refresh controls: LockViewUpdate suspends redraws and panel updates while a script makes many changes (especially when building library components), UnLockViewUpdate restores them, and GraphicallyInvalidate forces a full repaint of the sheet after modifications.
tools.notes: Always unlock in a Finally block; a locked document stays blank until unlocked.

tools.name: Schematic object id constants (eSchComponent, ePin, eWire, eBus, eBusEntry, eNetLabel, ePort, ePowerObject, eParameter, eDesignator, eSheetSymbol, eSheetEntry, eJunction, eLine, eRectangle, eLabel, eTextFrame, eNote, eNoERC, eParameterSet, eHarnessConnector, eHarnessEntry, eSignalHarness)
tools.description: TObjectId values for the schematic domain used by SchServer.SchObjectFactory and ISch_Iterator.AddFilter_ObjectSet: eSchComponent, ePin, eWire, eBus, eBusEntry, eNetLabel, ePort, ePowerObject, eParameter, eDesignator, eSheetSymbol, eSheetEntry, eSheetName, eSheetFileName, eJunction, eLine, ePolyline, ePolygon, eArc, eEllipticalArc, eEllipse, eRectangle, eRoundRectangle, eBezier, eLabel, eTextFrame, eNote, eImage, eSymbol (IEEE), eNoERC, eParameterSet, eCompileMask, eBlanket, eProbe, eHarnessConnector, eHarnessEntry, eSignalHarness, eOffSheetConnector, eTemplate, eDocument.
tools.notes: Child objects (pins, parameters) of components are reached with Cmp.SchIterator_Create, not the document iterator.

tools.name: ISch_NetLabel / ISch_Port / ISch_PowerObject
tools.description: Net identifier objects: ISch_NetLabel has Text, Location, Orientation (eRotate0/90/180/270), FontId, Color; ISch_Port has Name, IOType (ePortIOUnspecified, ePortIOOutput, ePortIOInput, ePortIOBidirectional), Style (ePortLeft, ePortRight, ePortLeftRight, ePortNone), Width, Alignment, Location, AreaColor/TextColor; ISch_PowerObject has Text (net name), Style (ePowerObjectStyle_Bar, _Circle, _Arrow, _Wave, _PowerGround, _SignalGround, _Earth, _GostArrow...), Orientation, Location, ShowNetName.
tools.usage: NL.Text := 'SDA';  Port.IOType := ePortIOBidirectional; Port.Style := ePortLeftRight;  PO.Text := 'GND'; PO.Style := ePowerObjectStyle_PowerGround;
tools.notes: Net labels must touch a wire hotspot (grid-aligned Location) to take effect.

tools.name: ISch_SheetSymbol / ISch_SheetEntry
tools.description: Hierarchy objects: ISch_SheetSymbol has SheetName and FileName child objects (SheetName.Text, FileName.Text), Location, XSize/YSize, AreaColor, and contains ISch_SheetEntry children (iterate with SheetSymbol.SchIterator_Create filtered on eSheetEntry). ISch_SheetEntry has Name, IOType, Side (eLeftSide/eRightSide/eTopSide/eBottomSide), DistanceFromTop, ArrowKind, HarnessType, Style.
tools.usage: SS := SchServer.SchObjectFactory(eSheetSymbol, eCreate_Default); SS.SheetName.Text := 'PSU'; SS.FileName.Text := 'PSU.SchDoc'; SS.XSize := MilsToCoord(1000); SS.YSize := MilsToCoord(600); SchDoc.RegisterSchObjectInContainer(SS);
tools.notes: After adding entries run Design > Synchronize Sheet Entries and Ports (or the Sch:SynchronizeSheetEntries process where available) to create matching ports.

tools.name: ISch_Designator and component parameter access (Cmp.Designator, Cmp.Comment, Cmp.GetState_SchPins, parameter iteration)
tools.description: ISch_Component exposes Designator and Comment as ISch_Designator/ISch_Parameter objects with Text, IsHidden, Location, Autoposition; other parameters are found by iterating the component with AddFilter_ObjectSet(MkSet(eParameter)) and reading Name/Text; pins via a child iterator on ePin (or GetState_SchPins). LibReference, LibraryPath/SourceLibraryName, CurrentPartID, PartCount, IsMirrored, Orientation, Location and ComponentKind complete the picture.
tools.usage: Cmp.Designator.Text := 'U3'; Cmp.Comment.Text := 'LM358'; PI := Cmp.SchIterator_Create; PI.AddFilter_ObjectSet(MkSet(eParameter)); P := PI.FirstSchObject; ... Cmp.SchIterator_Destroy(PI);
tools.notes: Adding a new parameter: P := SchServer.SchObjectFactory(eParameter, eCreate_Default); P.Name := ...; P.Text := ...; Cmp.AddSchObject(P).

tools.name: ISch_Lib (schematic library document API)
tools.description: Library-document interface (descendant of ISch_Document) for .SchLib scripts: CurrentSchComponent (focused symbol), SchLibIterator_Create/Destroy to walk all ISch_Component symbols, AddSchComponent/RemoveSchComponent, GetState_SchComponentCount, plus the normal factory/registration protocol to add pins, graphics and parameters to a symbol. Used for batch symbol generation and library audits.
tools.usage:
Lib := SchServer.GetCurrentSchDocument;  // when a .SchLib is active
LI := Lib.SchLibIterator_Create; LI.AddFilter_ObjectSet(MkSet(eSchComponent)); Sym := LI.FirstSchObject; ... Lib.SchIterator_Destroy(LI);
tools.notes: Check ObjectId or the document kind (DM_DocumentKind = 'SCHLIB') before casting to ISch_Lib.

tools.name: IProject.DM_Compile / DM_CompileEx / DM_NeedsCompile
tools.description: Compiles (validates) the project from a script so that nets, components and hierarchy are available through the Workspace Manager API: DM_Compile returns True on success; DM_CompileEx(All, Cancelled) forces full compilation; DM_NeedsCompile reports whether documents changed since the last compile. Violations are then listed via DM_ViolationCount / DM_Violations(i).
tools.usage: If Prj.DM_Compile Then ...;  Prj.DM_CompileEx(True, Cancelled);  If Prj.DM_NeedsCompile Then Prj.DM_Compile;
tools.notes: Equivalent GUI action: Project > Validate PCB Project.

tools.name: IProject.DM_ProjectFileName / DM_ProjectFullPath / DM_GetOutputPath / DM_SetOutputPath
tools.description: Project identity and output location: DM_ProjectFileName (name only), DM_ProjectFullPath (full path of the .PrjPcb), DM_GetOutputPath (the configured Project Outputs folder), DM_SetOutputPath and DM_InitializeOutputPath(OutputType) to create/return the folder for a given output type; also DM_ProjectTemplateLocation and DM_UserID.
tools.notes: Output path options are in Project Options > Options.

tools.name: IProject.DM_LogicalDocuments / DM_PhysicalDocuments / DM_GeneratedDocuments
tools.description: Document enumeration: DM_LogicalDocumentCount/DM_LogicalDocuments(i) return the source documents as listed in the project (each sheet once); DM_PhysicalDocumentCount/DM_PhysicalDocuments(i) return the compiled physical instances (one per channel of a multi-channel sheet); DM_GeneratedDocumentCount/DM_GeneratedDocuments(i) return generated outputs; DM_TopLevelLogicalDocument / DM_TopLevelPhysicalDocument and DM_PrimaryImplementationDocument (the PCB) locate key documents.
tools.usage: For i := 0 To Prj.DM_LogicalDocumentCount - 1 Do Doc := Prj.DM_LogicalDocuments(i);
tools.notes: Physical documents exist only after a successful DM_Compile.

tools.name: IProject.DM_AddSourceDocument / DM_RemoveSourceDocument / DM_IndexOfSourceDocument / DM_MoveSourceDocument
tools.description: Project membership editing: DM_AddSourceDocument(Filename) adds a document to the project (as Add Existing to Project does), DM_RemoveSourceDocument(Filename) removes it, DM_IndexOfSourceDocument returns its position, DM_MoveSourceDocument(Filename, NewIndex) reorders (affects sheet numbering order), DM_AddGeneratedDocument registers an output file. Save the project afterwards with WorkspaceManager:SaveObject ObjectKind=Project.
tools.notes: Paths may be relative to the project folder.

tools.name: IProject.DM_ProjectVariants / DM_CurrentProjectVariant (IProjectVariant)
tools.description: Variant access: DM_ProjectVariantCount and DM_ProjectVariants(i) return IProjectVariant objects (DM_Description, DM_VariationCount/DM_Variations(i) with per-component fitted state and alternate part/parameter variations), DM_CurrentProjectVariant is the active variant; DM_RemoveProjectVariant deletes one. Used to generate variant-aware reports from scripts.
tools.usage: For v := 0 To Prj.DM_ProjectVariantCount - 1 Do Variant := Prj.DM_ProjectVariants(v);
tools.notes: Variant definitions are edited in Project > Variants; the API is mainly read-oriented.

tools.name: IProject.DM_SearchPaths / DM_AddSearchPath / DM_ErrorLevels / DM_SetErrorLevels
tools.description: Project option access: DM_SearchPathCount/DM_SearchPaths(i) (ISearchPath with path and sub-folder flag) and DM_AddSearchPath(Path, IncludeSubFolders) manage Project Options > Search Paths; DM_ErrorLevels(ErrorKind) / DM_SetErrorLevels(ErrorKind, Level) read and set Error Reporting severities; DM_HierarchyMode/DM_SetHierarchyMode select net identifier scope; DM_ChannelDesignatorFormat and DM_ChannelRoomNamingStyle expose Multi-Channel settings; DM_EditOptions(PageName) opens the Project Options dialog.
tools.example:
Prj.DM_AddSearchPath(ExtractFilePath(Prj.DM_ProjectFullPath) + 'Models', True);
ResetParameters; AddStringParameter('ObjectKind', 'Project'); RunProcess('WorkspaceManager:SaveObject');
tools.notes: Error kind constants (TErrorKind) are numerous; read them from an existing project rather than hard-coding.

tools.name: IDocument.DM_FullPath / DM_FileName / DM_DocumentKind / DM_Project
tools.description: Basic document identity: DM_FullPath and DM_FileName give the path and name, DM_DocumentKind returns the kind string ('SCH', 'PCB', 'SCHLIB', 'PCBLIB', 'OUTPUTJOB', 'PCBDwf', 'BomDoc' ...), DM_Project returns the owning IProject, DM_DocumentIsLoaded/DM_LoadDocument control loading, DM_IsPrimaryImplementationDocument flags the PCB, and DM_UpdateDateModified marks changes.
tools.notes: Kind strings are upper-case for SCH/PCB and case-sensitive comparisons should use UpperCase.

tools.name: IDocument.DM_Nets / DM_NetCount (INet, INetItem)
tools.description: Compiled connectivity of a document (use the flattened top-level or physical document for the whole design): DM_NetCount and DM_Nets(i) return INet objects with DM_NetName, DM_PinCount/DM_Pins(i) (INetItem pins with DM_LogicalPartDesignator / DM_PhysicalPartDesignator and DM_PinNumber), DM_NetLabelCount/DM_NetLabels(i), DM_PortCount/DM_Ports(i), DM_PowerObjectCount, DM_NetClassCount; DM_NetClasses(i) at document level list classes. This is how the shipped ScripterProtelNetlist example builds a netlist.
tools.usage: Doc := Prj.DM_DocumentFlattened; For n := 0 To Doc.DM_NetCount - 1 Do Net := Doc.DM_Nets(n);
tools.notes: DM_DocumentFlattened is the compiled flat design (all sheets merged); per-sheet nets are local unless the scope makes them global.

tools.name: IDocument.DM_Components / DM_ComponentCount (IComponent, IPart)
tools.description: Compiled component list: DM_ComponentCount/DM_Components(i) return IComponent objects with DM_LogicalDesignator, DM_PhysicalDesignator, DM_Comment, DM_Description, DM_FootPrint, DM_LibReference, DM_PartCount/DM_Parts(i) (IPart with DM_PinCount/DM_Pins), DM_ParameterCount/DM_Parameters(i), DM_UniqueId and DM_ChannelIndex; DM_UniqueComponentCount/DM_UniqueComponents ignore multi-channel duplicates. Use the flattened or physical document for board-level designators.
tools.usage: For c := 0 To Flat.DM_ComponentCount - 1 Do Cmp := Flat.DM_Components(c);
tools.notes: This read-only view is ideal for custom BOMs; editing goes through the schematic API.

tools.name: IDocument hierarchy and multi-channel members (DM_ChildDocuments, DM_ParentDocuments, DM_SheetSymbols, DM_PhysicalRoomName, DM_ChannelIndex, DM_Parameters)
tools.description: Structure navigation: DM_ChildDocumentCount/DM_ChildDocuments(i) and DM_ParentDocumentCount/DM_ParentDocuments(i) walk the hierarchy; DM_SheetSymbolCount/DM_SheetSymbols(i) list sheet symbols (ISheetSymbol objects described by DM_LongDescriptorString); DM_PhysicalRoomName, DM_ChannelIndex, DM_ChannelPrefix, DM_CurrentInstanceNumber identify channel instances; DM_ParameterCount/DM_Parameters(i) give document parameters; DM_RoomCount/DM_Rooms, DM_ComponentClassCount/DM_ComponentClasses, DM_DifferentialPairCount/DM_DifferentialPairs, DM_RuleCount/DM_Rules expose generated classes/rules.
tools.usage: For k := 0 To Doc.DM_ChildDocumentCount - 1 Do Child := Doc.DM_ChildDocuments(k);
tools.notes: Call on DM_TopLevelPhysicalDocument to include every channel instance.

tools.name: PCB:Zoom (process)
tools.description: Zoom/redraw process of the PCB editor with an Action parameter: Redraw (refresh the view), All (fit document), In, Out, Area, Selected, Previous, Point; the documented example uses Action=Redraw and Action=All. Use it to refresh the display after scripted changes or to frame results.

parameters.name: Action
parameters.description: Redraw | All | In | Out | Area | Selected | Previous ...

tools.notes: Sch:Zoom is the schematic equivalent with the same Action values.

tools.name: PCB:DesignRuleCheck (process)
tools.description: Runs the Design Rule Checker on the active PCB. Without parameters it opens the Design Rule Checker dialog; parameters (as documented for the command) select what to check and report, e.g. the rule categories, online/batch behaviour, report creation and violation limits, mirroring the dialog's Report Options (CreateReportFile, CreateViolations, StopWhenViolationsFound). Used by release scripts before generating outputs.
tools.usage: RunProcess('PCB:DesignRuleCheck');   // opens the dialog; add parameters per the command reference to run silently

parameters.name: Report options
parameters.description: Create report file / violations, violation limit (see command reference for exact parameter names).

tools.example:
ResetParameters;
RunProcess('PCB:DesignRuleCheck');
tools.notes: For fully unattended DRC prefer an Output Job Validation output (Design Rules Check) generated through WorkspaceManager:GenerateReport or the OutJob processes.

tools.name: PCB:PlaceComponent (process)
tools.description: Launches the PCB Place Component command; with parameters it can pre-select the footprint and designator (Footprint, Designator, Comment, and library source parameters as listed in the command reference) so a script can place footprints interactively or from a library. Object-API alternative: create an IPCB_Component and add its primitives from a loaded IPCB_Library footprint.
tools.notes: Parameter names should be confirmed against the PCB commands reference for your version; the command is interactive (the footprint floats on the cursor).

tools.name: PCB:Export (process)
tools.description: Export process of the PCB editor covering the File > Export formats (STEP, Parasolid, DXF/DWG, IDF, VRML, PDF3D, Hyperlynx, Ansys EDB, PADS, Specctra ...); when run with the appropriate Format/FileName parameters it performs the export, otherwise it shows the export dialog. Commonly used from scripts to emit STEP files after placement changes.
tools.notes: STEP export options (holes, copper, components) are dialog settings; an OutJob Export STEP output is the reproducible alternative.

tools.name: PCB:Select / PCB:DeSelect (processes)
tools.description: Selection processes with an Object parameter mirroring Edit > Select / Deselect: All, Net, Connection, PhysicalConnection, ComponentConnections, AllOnLayer, InsideArea, OutsideArea, TouchingLine, TouchingRectangle, Free, ToggleSelection, plus Net=<name> for named nets in some versions. PCB:DeSelect with Object=All clears the selection, which scripts run before iterating SelectecObject.

parameters.name: Object
parameters.description: All | Net | Connection | PhysicalConnection | AllOnLayer | InsideArea | Free | ToggleSelection ...

tools.notes: Interactive variants (InsideArea, TouchingLine) wait for user input.

tools.name: Sch:PlacePart (process)
tools.description: Starts component placement in the schematic editor; parameters can pre-fill the Place Part settings (Library/library path, LibReference or Part name, Designator, Comment, Footprint) so the chosen symbol floats on the cursor ready to click, or the Components panel opens when parameters are absent. Object-API alternative: ISch_Document.PlaceSchComponent.

parameters.name: Designator / Comment / Footprint
parameters.description: Values applied to the placed part.

tools.notes: Exact parameter names are listed on the Sch:PlacePart command page for your version.

tools.name: Sch:Zoom / Sch:Annotate / Sch:PlaceWire / Sch:PlaceNetLabel / Sch:PlacePort (processes)
tools.description: Frequently used schematic processes: Sch:Zoom (Action=All|Redraw|In|Out|Area|Selected), Sch:Annotate (opens the Annotate dialog; with Action parameters runs quiet annotation), Sch:PlaceWire, Sch:PlaceBus, Sch:PlaceNetLabel, Sch:PlacePort, Sch:PlaceSheetSymbol, Sch:PlaceSheetEntry, Sch:PlaceLine and Sch:CreateSheetSymbolFromSheet / Sch:CreateSheetFromSheetSymbol, each corresponding to the Place/Design menu command of the same name.

parameters.name: Action (Sch:Zoom)
parameters.description: All | Redraw | In | Out | Area | Selected.

tools.notes: Placement processes are interactive; for silent object creation use the schematic object API.

tools.name: WorkspaceManager:OpenObject (process)
tools.description: Opens projects or documents: parameters ObjectKind (Project, Document, NewFromTemplate, ...), FileName (path), and options such as Kind/Template for new documents. The documented example creates a project from a template with Client.SendMessage('WorkspaceManager:OpenObject', 'OpenMode=NewFromTemplate | ObjectKind=Project', 1024, Nil).

parameters.name: FileName
parameters.description: Path of the object to open.

tools.notes: Client.OpenDocument(Kind, Path) is the object-API alternative for single documents.

tools.name: WorkspaceManager:SaveObject / WorkspaceManager:CloseObject (processes)
tools.description: Save and close processes with ObjectKind selecting the target: FocusedDocument, Project, FocusedProject, Document (with FileName), All; SaveObject supports SaveMode (Save, SaveAs, SaveCopyAs) with a FileName for the new path, CloseObject supports closing the focused document/project or all documents, prompting for unsaved changes unless suppressed. These are the script equivalents of File > Save / Save As / Close and Project > Close Project.
tools.notes: Confirm parameter spellings on the SaveObject/CloseObject command pages of your version.

tools.name: WorkspaceManager:GenerateReport (process)
tools.description: Generates project outputs (netlists, BOM/reports, prints) without the GUI: ObjectKind names the output family (e.g. Netlist), Index selects the specific generator/format in that family, ReturnGeneratedDocuments=True asks for the produced file names, which are read back with GetStringParameter('Result', ...) and GetStringParameter('File1', ...). Basis of scripted netlist exports; OutJob-based generation is preferred for full manufacturing sets.

parameters.name: Index
parameters.description: Ordinal of the generator within the family (order of the Design > Netlist For Project menu).

parameters.name: ReturnGeneratedDocuments
parameters.description: True to get result file names back.

tools.notes: Index numbering follows the installed netlisters, so verify on the target machine.

tools.name: WorkspaceManager:Compile (process)
tools.description: Compiles/validates a project or document from a script (Project > Validate PCB Project): parameters ObjectKind (Project, FocusedProject, Document) and Action (Compile) as documented in the WorkspaceManager commands reference. The object-API equivalent is IProject.DM_Compile, which also returns success and gives access to violations.
tools.notes: Prefer IProject.DM_Compile when you need the result; the process just triggers the GUI action.

tools.name: Client.SendMessage vs RunProcess parameter passing (GetStringParameter / AddIntegerParameter)
tools.description: Two ways to invoke processes: the parameter stack (ResetParameters, AddStringParameter, AddIntegerParameter, AddWordParameter, RunProcess, then GetStringParameter/GetIntegerParameter to read return values) or the one-liner Client.SendMessage('Server:Command', 'Param1=Value | Param2=Value', 255, Client.CurrentView) whose parameter string is pipe-separated. The stack form is required when return values are needed (e.g. GenerateReport); SendMessage suits VBScript/JScript and fire-and-forget commands.
tools.usage: ResetParameters; AddStringParameter('Name', 'Value'); RunProcess('Server:Command'); GetStringParameter('Result', S);   |   Client.SendMessage('Server:Command', 'Name=Value | Name2=Value2', 255, Client.CurrentView);
tools.notes: The process must be one the current view/server can handle; PCB: processes need a PCB document focused.

tools.name: Customized command running a script (ScriptingSystem:RunScript from menus, toolbars and hotkeys)
tools.description: To give a script a menu entry, toolbar button or hotkey, create a command in the Customizing Editor with Process ScriptingSystem:RunScript and Parameters ProjectName=<path to .PrjScr>|ProcName=<Unit.pas>Procedure, optionally with an icon and shortcut; the script project must be accessible at that path (or be part of the open project group). RunScriptText runs literal statements instead.
tools.usage: Right-click menu bar > Customize > New command: Process=ScriptingSystem:RunScript, Parameters=ProjectName=D:\Scripts\Tools.PrjScr|ProcName=Tools.pas>RenumberVias

parameters.name: ProjectName
parameters.description: Full path of the script project.

parameters.name: ProcName
parameters.description: Unit file name, '>' and procedure name.

tools.example:
Parameters: ProjectName=C:\Users\Public\Documents\Altium\Scripts\PCB\Vias.PrjScr|ProcName=Vias.pas>TentSmallVias
Shortcut: Ctrl+Alt+T
tools.notes: Scripts run this way have no debugger; test from the Scripts panel first.
